text:
Josh Anderson was scoring at a career pace for Montreal, seven goals in 16 games, and then missed Saturday's win over Toronto. RotoWire listed him as unavailable, part of several lineup changes Martin St-Louis made. We don't have a clear reason, and we won't guess at one.

The goals have been real chances: seven on 5.1 expected (the quality of his chances). His shooting is hot, 21% against a typical 12 to 17%, and Montreal has scored 7.6 more goals than expected with him on the ice while getting only 47% of the five-on-five chances. His goals have still been worth 1.09 wins by our numbers, 52nd in the league.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the front of the net often (81st percentile) while carrying the puck in on only 32% of his entries, the classic power-forward game. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. Our projection sees about 22 goals, which would be his best year in a while if he's back in the lineup soon.
